transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (NovaBridge CTO), Ellen Ko (Platform PM), Tom Wu (Infra), Priya Rao (Security)

Summary:
Quick sync to align on NovaBridge marketplace listing requirements and the on‑prem connector conformance plan. Main goals: packaging for marketplace, KMS/SSO compatibility, network topology & peering, and a dry‑run on staging to validate installation and perf.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing checklist and reference architecture
- On‑prem connector packaging (Helm, OCI images, runbooks)
- Security: KMS, SSO, audit logs, SOC2 artefacts
- Performance conformance tests: latency SLOs and acceptance criteria
- Rollout plan and next steps

Action items (as discussed in call): see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for hopping on. quick intros?
[00:06] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): yeah samir here, sorry if my mic is a bit rough, hello.
[00:09] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): ellen, platform PM.
[00:11] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): tom infra.
[00:13] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): priya security.
[00:15] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): diego here, i'll cover the connector and benchmarks.
[00:18] Rina Patel (Redwood): rina, solution eng, packaging and ops.
[00:20] Maya Chen (Redwood): quick recap of agenda—marketplace packaging, onprem connector conformance, perf criteria, and scheduling a dry run.

[02:05] Maya Chen (Redwood): Ellen you sent over the marketplace questionnaire earlier, we reviewed, and there are three pcs where we usually see friction: the manifest metadata, installer artifacts (helm vs tarball), and the KMS integration notes. can you confirm you prefer helm chart distribution for your internal catalog?
[02:26] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): yes helm is easiest. we have an internal registry that consumes OCI artifacts and OCI helm charts. tarballs are a pain for our SREs.
[02:35] Rina Patel (Redwood): great, we can provide an OCI helm chart + signed image. we'll include a values.yaml with the typical modes: hosted fallback, dedicated pool, and pure on‑prem.

[04:01] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): regarding network: do you require inbound from the vendor or does the connector initiate outbound? our compliance requires minimal inbound.
[04:16] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): connector is outbound first. for managed control plane we do a TLS tunneled control channel outbound. for fully air‑gapped installs there is an on‑prem control plane package, but that's heavier. for marketplace listing we should document both.
[04:35] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): ok outbound is fine. we'll need the exact egress FQDNs and ports for the staging run.

[06:40] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): security stuff: we need to validate KMS compatibility, bring‑your‑own KMS (BYOK), SSO via SAML, and audit log retention. SOC2 attestation is also required for vendor listing in our procurement. can you walk through docs?
[06:58] Maya Chen (Redwood): absolutely. we have a vendor pack: SOC2 type II PDF, OIDC/SAML integration guide, and an audit logging guide. for KMS we support customer‑managed keys with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and an HSM connector. for on‑prem we can point to our KMS shim that accepts KMIP and Vault.
[07:20] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): KMIP would be ideal—our HSM team prefers that. do you have an example config?
[07:27] Rina Patel (Redwood): yes we'll attach a sample kmip.yaml and a runbook for key rotation. note the shim has some limitations with rotated keys and caching—will document TTLs.

[09:10] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): performance is big for us. our product surfaces mem‑caching and low latency LLM responses for in‑app assistants. what are typical p95/p99 numbers on dedicated vs on‑prem? and can you do quantized models?
[09:30] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): dedicated GPUs in our Dedicated product hit sub‑200ms p95 on common 2k token prompts for the 13B open model variants with batching disabled. p99 can vary; for strict p99 SLOs we recommend autoscaling pools and prefix/KV cache. for on‑prem it depends entirely on HW and if you enable int8 quantization we can reduce memory and latency but sometimes quality changes. we'll propose a benchmark matrix.
[09:58] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): great. can we make that the acceptance criteria for the marketplace listing? like p95 < 250ms for <= 512 tokens on a 8‑gpu node?
[10:10] Maya Chen (Redwood): that's reasonable as long as the node spec is defined. we'll include exact node types in the refarch.

[12:00] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): question on routing: if you publish to our internal catalog and offer hosted fallback, how do we guarantee data residency? we can't allow tokenized content leaving our VPC.
[12:18] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): we support strict no‑egress mode for private deployments; the fallback policy can be disabled. for hosted fallback we only recommend it for non‑sensitive workloads and we mark it explicitly in the manifest.
[12:35] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): so for our catalog listing we want a manifest flag 'no_fallback' to be required.
[12:40] Rina Patel (Redwood): we'll add that to the packaging checklist and the values.yaml default will set no_fallback = true.

[15:05] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): network diagram: we'll share our staging VPC CIDRs. what peering options do you support—VPC peering, PrivateLink, or site‑to‑site?
[15:20] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): we support VPC peering for AWS, PrivateLink for AWS partners, and IPsec site‑to‑site for onprem. for marketplace we usually document PrivateLink as it's easiest for customers who want vendor control plane access.
[15:35] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): ok we'll check if PrivateLink works with our infra team. I'll add that to the action items.

[18:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): packaging specifics—what we need from NovaBridge: registry credentials for staging, acceptance test cluster kubeconfig, and target node types. we provide the chart and a validation job.
[18:18] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): we can do a short lived service account for staging, but we need an inventory of what the validation job will try to create. no privileged cluster wide stuff without us signing off.
[18:33] Rina Patel (Redwood): validation job is namespace scoped, creates a Deployment and runs a test client that fires 100 requests and measures latencies. must be non‑privileged. we'll share the manifest in the next 48h.

[21:00] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): about licensing—if we list in our internal marketplace, do we expect the Redwood pricing model or is it packaged as a BYOL with support contract?
[21:16] Maya Chen (Redwood): we support both. for marketplace listings we typically provide a partner priced SKU that integrates with your billing, or we can do BYOL for enterprise customers. we'll coordinate with GTM later.

[23:50] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): audits—do you provide verifiable tamper‑evident logs? our compliance needs show proof of access and change history.
[24:05] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): yes we surface audit logs to an external syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver endpoint, and we can include signed log delivery. retention is configurable and we can support IL4/IL5 patterns for enterprise.

[26:40] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): small nit: our internal catalog requires icons and marketing blurb. who owns that content?
[26:50] Maya Chen (Redwood): we can provide a short blurb and multiple icon sizes; marketing will sign off but we'll draft an initial version and attach it to the checklist.

[29:00] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): on the on‑prem connector—how do upgrades work? we prefer declarative upgrades controlled by our SREs.
[29:12] Rina Patel (Redwood): helm upgrades, operator‑style lifecycle is supported. we ship migration hooks in the chart. we also publish image digests so you can pin versions. for rollback we support the last known good.

[31:10] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): for the conformance dry‑run, what's the test matrix? we'd like to include: install verification, KMS key rotation test, SSO login test, a perf run with synthetic prompts, and failure/injection test (network loss).
[31:30] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): yep that's our standard matrix. we'll add an additional test for prefix/KV cache correctness under sequential sessions. also a compatibility test for your HSM integration.

[34:05] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): note: our legal also will ask for data processing addendum (DPA) and standard contractual clauses; we flagged that to procurement.
[34:20] Maya Chen (Redwood): noted, i'll loop in our legal and send a template DPA and standard clauses.

[36:00] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): do you have a recommended staging size for the perf tests? we're thinking an 8‑gpu node to mimic our planned prod.
[36:12] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): 8x A10G style or similar will be fine for our 13B variant tests. if you plan to test 70B we should discuss memory and NVMe configs.

[38:40] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): any special kernel modules or host tweaks? our security team doesn't want unnecessary host changes.
[38:55] Rina Patel (Redwood): minimal; mostly sysctl tweaks for latency. we'll document them and make them opt‑in. the connector doesn't require privileged mode.

[40:30] Maya Chen (Redwood): ok timeline check—if we get the creds and diagrams by 8/28 we can prepare the chart and validation job by 8/31, tests run the week of 9/8, and a short results readout 9/12. does that align?
[40:50] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): that works. our procurement lead needs some slack but staging and infra teams are available.

[42:20] Priya Rao (NovaBridge): small question—are there known incompatibilities with our GKE on‑prem offering? last time we saw issues in node feature gates.
[42:33] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): we've validated on GKE‑on‑prem for 1.24 and 1.25; feature gates like HugePages need to be documented, but mostly it's not an issue. we'll include a compatibility matrix.

[44:40] Maya Chen (Redwood): competitor note: CloudCorpAI has a similar marketplace approach but their on‑prem installer required privileged daemonset which is a no for many customers. we'll highlight our non‑privileged approach.

[46:10] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): good to know. one last thing—do you have an example manifest that sets no_fallback and BYOK?
[46:22] Rina Patel (Redwood): yes, we'll attach a sample manifest with keys: no_fallback: true, kms_provider: kmip, imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent.

[48:00] Tom Wu (NovaBridge): for the perf benchmarks Diego, will you share the script and the analyzer so we can run it ourselves?
[48:10] Diego Alvarez (Redwood): yep. mini benchmark script and an analyzer that outputs p50/p95/p99 and token‑throughput—will upload to the shared doc. it's a simple Python script that hits the gRPC endpoint and records latencies.

[50:05] Samir Patel (NovaBridge): ok recap for our side: we'll provide registry creds, kubeconfig for staging, VPC diagram and whether PrivateLink is acceptable, and HSM contact for KMIP. procurement will review DPA.
[50:22] Maya Chen (Redwood): and recap from us: we'll send packaging checklist, helm chart draft, manifest sample, SOC2 & security pack, and the benchmark script. we will schedule the dry run week of 9/8.

[52:00] Ellen Ko (NovaBridge): and we'll confirm dates by 8/28. thanks everyone.
[52:08] Maya Chen (Redwood): perfect thanks all. we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invites.
[52:15] (meeting ends)
